title: Corma Receives $125 Million to Train Foundation Models for Defensive Cybersecurity
content_md: Cybersecurity startup Corma has raised $125 million in a Series A funding round, bringing the total raised to $185 million and its valuation to $1 billion. Led by NEA, the investment round saw additional support from previous backers Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, and Coatue. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, Corma emerged from stealth mode in August with a frontier foundation model specifically designed for defensive cybersecurity. Corma says AI’s offensive capabilities have grown exponentially over the past several months, while its defensive capabilities have not, and it aims to fill that gap. The startup trains frontier foundation models and deploys them as AI agents alongside existing security tools to audit security data and correlate signals across environments to improve defenses and help security teams respond to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks. “Cybersecurity is now a battle of intelligence against intelligence, and Black October made that impossible to ignore,” said Corma co-founder and CEO Alon Pluda. “Since we came out of stealth, demand from the world’s largest organizations has been overwhelming, and one of our hardest problems has been securing capacity fast enough to keep up with the demand,” Pluda added.
